correctness.rationale: With ambient Haar measure divided by 2π, the diagonal is t=2a/π and the first two off-diagonal coefficients are cu and v=d(2u²−1), respectively. Endpoint contact has no effect. In the reflection decomposition the eigenvalues are t−v and t+(v±H)/2, with H²=v²+8c²u². The lower symmetric branch is minimal: for v≤0 this is immediate, and for v>0 one has v≤d|u|<c|u| and hence H>3v. Subtracting (v+2d)² from H² yields 8u²(c²−d²), and v+2d>0. This gives the exact deficit and strictness for any nonantipodal configuration, including the endpoint-contact placement. At u=0 the spectrum is t−d,t,t+d; t−d>0, and the inverse norm is the reciprocal square root, with equality on its least-eigenvalue mode. Since u²=(θ−π/2)²+O((θ−π/2)^4) and the rationalized denominator tends to 2d, the sharp local coefficient is 4 sin³(a)/(π cos(a)) at fixed a. The small-a asymptotics follow by expanding sin(2a). The accompanying checker was inspected, not executed; its trace, determinant and finite grid checks are consistency diagnostics only.

value.rationale: For two movable exposures of prescribed width, least squared singular value is the sharp stability objective, not a freely chosen spectral statistic. The result gives the unique acquisition geometry, an exact off-optimum performance penalty, and the reconstruction cost even for narrow arcs. Those numerical laws are useful without a higher-band extension or optimization over arbitrary masks.
